children: The dollar could gain if elevated energy prices support expectations for interest-rate rises across the G-10, HSBC strategist Daragh Maher says in a note. In this scenario, currencies should respond more to their exposure to the energy price shock rather than rate expectations, he says. "On that basis, the dollar could benefit from the U.S. economy's greater energy self-sufficiency and resilience relative to more import-dependent economies, particularly the eurozone and the U.K." (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
